text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a sudden spike in eu-rt-1 p95 and increased connection resets, started ~09:12 UTC. Error rate ~10%. Starting a quick bridge: https://meet.redwood-internal/bridge/xyz123 :rotating_light:

ops-bot: Bridge created by alex — https://meet.redwood-internal/bridge/xyz123. Recording enabled.

maya: joining now. scope — serving, infra, or both?

alex: looks like serving nodes hitting TCP RSTs from the nginx LB. p95 from ~120ms -> ~420ms. Logs show repeated `connection reset by peer` from redis KV client. snippet: ```ERR: connection reset by peer at kv_client.go:214
store: kv/cache: evict loop triggered```

sam: pinging infra team, tagging jordan for redis scaling

jordan: I'm on redis. one replica OOM-killed a few mins ago and is behind. Recovering now. Increasing maxmemory-policy to volatile-lru temporarily. Can someone drain traffic off 10.3.5.12?

maya: draining now via `redwood infra route set --drain 10.3.5.12` — will confirm when cordoned

alex: agenda for the ad-hoc: 1) confirm failover healthy 2) validate kvcache eviction pattern 3) quick mitigations (drain, bump mem, fallback model) 4) owners + postmortem actions

jordan: repl sync finished at 09:20 UTC, pushing new memory limits. still watching sync lag, ETA ~5m

sam: :thumbsup: please paste any error logs to the bridge. I'll sketch an incident note in /incidents/ after we stabilize

maya: quick question — do we want an automatic fallback to a smaller model for this route? I can flip routing policy to `fallback=llama-mini` for 10m if needed

alex: yes, plan: only enable fallback if p95 remains >300ms after drain. I'll create a 5% canary to fallback now: `redwood route update --canary 5% --fallback llama-mini`

ops-bot: Canary update recorded. run id=canary-2026-03-17-0918

jordan: root cause looks like a cache warm job that blasted large prefixes and triggered eviction pressure leading to OOM. I'll add a throttle and open a PR for the rate-limiter.

alex: watching metrics on the bridge. If p95 is <200ms in 10m we close. Thanks everyone — continuing in the bridge for now.

(Notes: added short-term mitigations: drained 10.3.5.12, bumped redis memory policy, enabled 5% canary fallback. Owners: jordan (redis), maya (routing), sam (incident doc), alex (triage lead).)
